metadata.documentation_strategy: Evidence-first: source and executable configuration take precedence over historical prose.
metadata.prototype_disclaimer: Research and demonstration prototype; not a production antivirus, EDR, or safe malware detonation service.
metadata.unknown_value_policy: Use Not recorded, Not available in this branch, or Requires team confirmation instead of guessing.

frontend.title: Frontend dashboard
frontend.purpose: Provide account access, executable or URL submission, scan progress, and report history views.
present_implementation: Static HTML, CSS, and browser JavaScript served by the backend or a separate development server.
Registration, login, logout, guest access, file selection, drag-and-drop, URL submission, polling, and stage progress display are connected to backend APIs.
The reports page contains pagination scaffolding but uses an empty in-memory array and does not call the scan-history endpoint.
interfaces: Calls /api/auth/register, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, and /api/auth/me with cookies.
Calls POST /api/samples for multipart uploads, POST /api/links for URL submissions, and GET /api/samples/:id while polling.
Does not currently call GET /api/samples to populate report history.
dependencies: Modern browser with Fetch, FormData, and JavaScript enabled.
Sentinel backend at the same origin or http://localhost:3000 with an allowed CORS origin.
configuration: Backend CORS_ORIGINS controls credentialed development origins.

inventory: No dedicated browser or frontend unit-test suite is present.
Backend auth and API tests exercise the endpoints consumed by the frontend.
observed: No browser automation was run during the 2026-11-03 documentation update.

limitations: The reports page is not integrated with scan history.
No detailed report viewer renders stored stage reports.
Client-side file validation checks only the .exe extension; the backend accepts the uploaded file and the analyzer decides whether it is a PE.
Accessibility and cross-browser behavior have not been formally tested.
risks: Rendered stage state is only as complete as backend results; optional or absent stages appear skipped.
Inline scripts and alert-based validation limit maintainability and accessibility.

evidence.note: Shared API, authentication, upload, link, and polling helpers.

backend.title: Backend API and orchestration
backend.purpose: Accept submissions, manage accounts and sessions, persist scan state, queue work, run pipeline stages, and serve the dashboard.
present_implementation: Express API with stable JSON errors, multipart upload handling, URL validation, authentication, SQLite or PostgreSQL persistence, and an in-process database-backed job queue.
Signature and static-analysis stages run by default; sandbox plus behavioral ML are enabled by SANDBOX_URL; LLM/threat intelligence is enabled by LLM_DIR.
Static ML is explicitly not present in the pipeline stage list.
The mock static analyzer is the default so local startup does not require pefile.
interfaces: GET /api/health
POST /api/auth/register, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout; GET /api/auth/me
POST /api/samples, POST /api/links, GET /api/samples, GET /api/samples/:id
Python analyzer subprocess emitting one JSON report on stdout.
Optional multipart sandbox /detonate call, behavioral-ML JSON HTTP call, and Python LLM bridge.
dependencies: Node.js with express, multer, dotenv, better-sqlite3, pg, and supertest.
Python 3 for the configured analyzer and LLM bridge.
SQLite by default or PostgreSQL when DATABASE_URL is set.
configuration: DATABASE_PATH or DATABASE_URL plus DATABASE_SSL and DATABASE_POOL_SIZE

inventory: Eight Node test files cover API, authentication, queueing, catalog validation, HTTP stages, sandbox/ML adapters, LLM stage behavior, and the real analyzer boundary.
Real-analyzer tests are conditionally skipped when pefile is unavailable.
observed: npm test did not start on 2026-11-03 because the available Windows npm shim reported that WSL 1 is unsupported.
historical: backend/README.md records prior passing backend results, but those counts were not re-verified in this environment.

limitations: Static ML is not wired into the pipeline.
The default analyzer is a mock unless ANALYZER_SCRIPT_PATH is changed.
Sandbox, behavioral ML, and LLM stages depend on external or absent components.
The in-process queue does not coordinate execution across multiple backend processes; worker ownership avoids processing another host's uploads.
Guest scanning is permitted by default.
risks: Uploaded files are stored on the backend host and require an operational retention and deletion policy.
COOKIE_SECURE defaults to false for local HTTP and must be enabled behind HTTPS.
Optional integrations can fail independently and leave a scan completed with failed stages.

evidence.note: Actual stage ordering and feature gates.

malware_detection.title: Static malware detection and PE evidence
malware_detection.purpose: Produce bounded, schema-validated PE metadata, hashes, strings, imports, resources, entropy, reputation, and optional YARA evidence.
present_implementation: Python CLI reads a bounded, consistent byte capture and emits report contract 1.2.0 as JSON.
PE extraction includes headers, sections and permissions, imports and delay imports, resources, bounded strings, parser warnings, and SHA-256.
Optional offline reputation cache and trusted YARA rule file enrich the report without network access during analysis.
Schema validation, integration verification, cache update, and YARA helper tools are present.
interfaces: python3 malware_detection/analyze.py <file> writes one JSON object to stdout and errors to stderr.
--hash-cache or STATIC_HASH_DB selects the offline reputation database.
--yara-rules or STATIC_YARA_RULES selects a trusted YARA source file.
backend/src/analyzer/runAnalyzer.js consumes schema versions 1.0.0 through 1.2.0.
dependencies: Optional yara-python for real YARA scanning.
configuration: Default maximum input size is documented and enforced by the analyzer CLI.
STATIC_HASH_DB and STATIC_YARA_RULES may replace CLI options.
YARA includes are disabled and scan timeout must be positive.

inventory: Six Python test modules cover bounded capture, extraction, report contract, consumers, reputation, and YARA behavior.
observed: The suite could not import on 2026-11-03 because pefile is not installed in the active Python environment.
historical: The component form and README record earlier passing results; they are historical evidence only for this update.

limitations: Static evidence is not a final malicious/benign verdict.
Offline reputation coverage depends entirely on the supplied cache.
YARA coverage depends on trusted user-supplied rules and the optional engine.
The backend defaults to its mock analyzer instead of this component.
risks: Parsing hostile files requires bounded inputs and patched dependencies.
A match-free report means no configured evidence matched; it does not prove a file is benign.

machine_learning.title: Behavioral feature extraction and machine learning
machine_learning.purpose: Normalize sandbox telemetry, produce behavioral features and heuristic risk, train optional classifier/anomaly models, serve inference, and evaluate labeled data.
present_implementation: Report parser validates current sandbox and legacy shapes and produces nine behavioral features.
Heuristic risk scoring is available without trained models.
Random Forest classifier and Isolation Forest training scripts save joblib artifacts.
CLI and ThreadingHTTPServer inference support optional classifier and anomaly artifacts.
Evaluation reports classification or anomaly metrics from supplied labeled JSON records.
interfaces: ML/predict.py reads a report from --file or stdin, or serves POST JSON on /, /analyze, and /analyze-report.
The backend adapter maps sandbox output to the ML report shape and calls BEHAVIORAL_ML_URL.
Training scripts expect JSON arrays containing reports and labels; evaluation expects a saved .joblib model.
configuration: Default malicious threshold comes from ML/config.py.

inventory: ML/test_report_parser.py contains 15 tests for normalization, validation, feature behavior, persistence evidence, and CLI/HTTP model parity.
observed: The suite could not import on 2026-11-03 because joblib is not installed in the active Python environment.

limitations: No dataset, trained model, model card, or evaluation output is committed.
The scripts do not implement a static-PE classifier for the malware_detection report.
Backend integration is behavioral only and requires the sandbox stage.
Held-out-family evaluation has not been evidenced in this branch.
risks: Heuristic risk is not a validated probability and must not be reported as trained-model performance.
Model quality, class balance, leakage, and licensing cannot be assessed without dataset provenance and artifacts.

evidence.note: Normalization, behavioral feature extraction, and heuristic risk.

dynamic_analysis.title: Dynamic sandbox integration
dynamic_analysis.purpose: Detonate files in an isolated, revertible environment and return runtime telemetry for behavioral scoring and reporting.
present_implementation: Backend multipart sandbox client, non-overlap lock, response checks, telemetry-shape adapter, feature gate, and mock-service tests are present.
The referenced dynamic_telemetry sandbox implementation, VM setup, snapshot lifecycle, guest instrumentation, and Sysmon collection code are not present in this branch.
interfaces: When SANDBOX_URL is set, the backend POSTs the sample and detonation timeout to /detonate.
The adapter expects usable telemetry and converts known sandbox field names to the ML service shape.
Links do not run through the sandbox stage.
dependencies: External sandbox HTTP service and a safely isolated Windows VM.

inventory: backend/test/sandboxStages.test.js covers client errors, timeouts, serialization, non-overlap, adapters, and pipeline behavior with mock HTTP services.
observed: Node tests did not start in the current WSL 1/npm environment. No real VM safety or detonation test was run.

limitations: No runnable sandbox implementation or environment definition exists in this branch.
Network isolation, reset behavior, sample transfer, log export, and host containment are not verified.
Remote-thread telemetry may be absent and is represented as zero with adapter notes.
risks: Real malware execution is unsafe without independently validated containment and restoration.
A malformed or empty telemetry response must fail the stage rather than be scored as benign.

evidence.note: Sandbox HTTP client and serialization lock.

llm_threat_intelligence.title: LLM and threat-intelligence integration
llm_threat_intelligence.purpose: Build bounded evidence input, enrich indicators, and eventually generate an evidence-grounded explanation with MITRE ATT&CK mappings.
present_implementation: Backend adapter collects bounded earlier-stage evidence and filters selected standalone IP indicators when they are private, loopback, or link-local.
Submitted URLs and raw telemetry fields remain in the prepared report and are not redacted before the Python bridge.
Python bridge imports an external llm-threat-intelligence directory and returns its threat-intelligence results and prompt.
Pipeline stage ordering and independent failure behavior are implemented when LLM_DIR is configured.
The external component is absent from this branch and the backend README states that it does not call an LLM or generate an explanation yet.
interfaces: LLM_DIR enables the stage and points to the external component directory.
backend/scripts/llm_bridge.py receives JSON on stdin and returns JSON on stdout.
The stage receives signature, static-analysis, sandbox, and behavioral-ML reports when available.
dependencies: Python 3 and an external llm-threat-intelligence component.
Any model/provider SDK and API credentials are not defined in this branch.
configuration: Provider, model, prompt version, temperature, retry policy, and token/cost controls are not recorded.

inventory: backend/test/llmStage.test.js covers indicator filtering, truncation, bridge failures, ordering, link input, and independent stage failure using fixtures/mocks.
observed: Node tests did not start in the current WSL 1/npm environment. No real provider or MITRE mapping validation was run.

limitations: No LLM provider, model, credentials, prompt artifact, explanation schema, or MITRE mapping implementation is available in this branch.
No hallucination, citation, redaction, cost, or mapping-accuracy evaluation is evidenced.
Input bounding reduces volume but is not a complete sensitive-data policy; submitted URLs and raw telemetry can still be forwarded without redaction.
risks: Sending telemetry or indicators to an external service may disclose sensitive data.
Ungrounded explanations or ATT&CK mappings could mislead users without evidence citations and human review.

FR01.requirement: Accept executable files through web upload or API.
FR01.gap: Backend test execution was not observed in the current environment; server-side PE or extension rejection is delegated to analysis rather than upload validation.

FR02.requirement: Query file hashes against a known signature database.
FR02.gap: The default backend catalog contains safe test indicators, no production feed is selected, and the analyzer's reputation/YARA evidence is only used when the real analyzer is configured.

FR03.requirement: Compute a static ML malicious-probability score.
FR03.gap: No static-feature model, training dataset, model artifact, or static_ml pipeline stage exists; current ML features are behavioral.

FR04.requirement: Detonate unknown binaries within an isolated sandbox.
FR04.gap: Only the backend client and mock tests are present; the VM, detonation API, reset lifecycle, and isolation validation are absent.

FR05.requirement: Compute a behavioral ML risk score from recorded runtime activity.
FR05.gap: Behavioral scoring code is present, but end-to-end operation requires the absent sandbox and no trained model artifact is supplied.

FR06.requirement: Generate an automated LLM report mapped to MITRE ATT&CK tactics.
FR06.gap: The external component is absent and no LLM explanation or MITRE mapping is generated by code in this branch.

FR07.requirement: Display scores, telemetry, and generated reports in a unified dashboard.
FR07.gap: The home page shows stage progress, but report history is disconnected and no detailed telemetry/report view is implemented.

FR08.requirement: Log historical scan results for benchmarking and validation.
FR08.gap: Persistence and paged retrieval exist, but no export or benchmarking workflow consumes the history in this branch.

NFR Safety.requirement: Isolate the sandbox network and host and restore a known state.
NFR Safety.gap: Client behavior is tested with mocks, but actual VM containment, networking, sample handling, and snapshot restoration are not present or verified.

NFR Explainability.requirement: Report feature importance and connect explanations to observed evidence.
NFR Explainability.gap: Evidence lists and static facts exist, but trained-model feature importance and LLM explanations with citations do not.

NFR Usability.requirement: Make the dashboard understandable to non-expert analysts.
NFR Usability.gap: The progress display has plain-language states, but report presentation, accessibility, and usability have not been completed or evaluated.

NFR Performance.requirement: Return static results within an interactive demonstration timeframe.
NFR Performance.gap: Timeouts and concurrency limits exist, but no latency target, load test, or current benchmark result is recorded.

NFR Maintainability.requirement: Keep a modular Git-based architecture with explicit contracts.
NFR Maintainability.gap: Cross-component contracts still disagree in places and the optional component source trees are not available on this branch.

verification.result: Tests did not start; the available npm shim reported WSL 1 is unsupported and could not determine the Node.js installation directory.
Six test modules failed to import because pefile is not installed; no assertions ran.
The test module failed to import because joblib is not installed; no assertions ran.

risks.description: No sandbox implementation or containment evidence is present in this branch.
risks.impact: Critical if real malware is executed under an assumed but unverified isolation boundary.
risks.likelihood: Medium if the prototype is demonstrated with real malware.
risks.mitigation: Use inert fixtures only until VM networking, host isolation, sample handling, and snapshot restoration are independently validated.

risks.description: Static ML is not wired and dynamic/LLM components are absent or optional.
risks.impact: The conceptual layered pipeline cannot run end to end from this branch.
risks.mitigation: Present the default signature plus mock static-analysis path honestly and track each optional integration separately.

risks.description: No dataset provenance, trained artifacts, or benchmark results are committed.
risks.impact: Accuracy, bias, leakage, family generalization, and licensing cannot be assessed.
risks.mitigation: Create dataset and model cards before reporting classifier performance; retain exact split and reproduction commands.

risks.description: Uploads, telemetry, URLs, hashes, and account records may contain sensitive data.
risks.impact: Local persistence or external enrichment could disclose information.
risks.likelihood: Medium when used beyond inert demonstrations.
risks.mitigation: Define retention, deletion, access, redaction, and external-data policies before deployment; do not commit secrets or samples.

risks.description: Several suites could not run in the documentation environment.
risks.impact: Current branch behavior is less certain than historical records imply.
risks.mitigation: Run Node tests under supported Node/WSL and install documented Python dependencies in an isolated environment before release claims.
